diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/6 is experiencing a port-level outage affecting all observed ONUs on the port. The OLT and router remain healthy, while every probed ONU on EPON0/6 is offline and the OLT health check identifies a failure associated with this PON.
evidence: The mass-offline trigger reports 29 affected ONUs on the same OLT, matching the 29 customers assigned to EPON0/6.
All seven listed ONUs on EPON0/6 are offline in both stored state and the live PON probe, indicating a shared infrastructure fault rather than an individual ONU fault.
The OLT is reachable by ping and SNMP, responds to the OID walk, and has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime; this rules out an OLT-wide failure.
The subscriber router is reachable with a healthy heartbeat, normal CPU, memory, and temperature; this rules out a router outage.
Customer VLAN 1066 is present and matches the expected VLAN, so provisioning or VLAN 46 issues are not indicated.
RADIUS data is present and consistent with CRM, and session activity is normal rather than flapping; authentication is not the cause.
Historical optical telemetry was healthy: RX was approximately -20 dBm, TX approximately +2.35 dBm, distance remained constant at 88, and TX bias stayed within the healthy range.
The current zero or null optical readings represent no reading because the ONUs are offline, not strong or degraded optical levels.
The OLT has 38 offline customers overall, but the 29 simultaneous outages concentrated on EPON0/6 are well beyond the normal background offline rate and identify the affected PON port.

remediation.action: Escalate to access-network operations immediately. Check EPON0/6 optics, port alarms, feeder fibre, patching, and the associated splitter path; clean/reseat connectors and test optical levels. If the fibre path is healthy, reset or move the ONUs to a spare PON port and replace the failed PON interface or line card if required. Recheck ONU registration and customer service after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/6 has failed, taking 28 of its 29 customers offline simultaneously 80 minutes ago. The twenty-ninth ONU had already been offline for three days from an unrelated individual fault and is not part of this event.
expected_reasoning: Every ONU on EPON0/6 now returns responds true with online 0
28 of the 29 stopped within the same minute, 80 minutes ago
One ONU on the port last held a session three days ago, so it was already down before this event
That ONU's separate history excludes it from this incident's affected set
OLT ping and SNMP succeed and the other seven ports are serving normally
The failure boundary follows EPON0/6 exactly
PON port traffic has collapsed from 231 Mbps average to 8 Mbps
distractors: The trigger states 29 offline, inviting that number to be reported as the blast radius
All 29 look identical in current state and only history separates them
